title: WPMS/90/2007 of GOVIND RAM Vs THIRD F.T.C/ A.D.J and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 90 of 2007
Govind Ram
 ÖÖÖÖ.Petitioner
Versus
III F.T.C./Additional District Judge, Haridwar and
others
 ÖÖ...Respondents
Present : Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Ashutosh Thakral, Advocate for the private
respondents.

Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 This is a matter arising out of a proceeding
under the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of
Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 (from hereinafter
referred to as the Act). The premises in question is in
Haridwar. Two rooms of the premises in question are
already allotted in favour of the present petitioner.
Another two rooms of the building were declared vacant,
which were subsequently allotted by the Rent Control
and Eviction Officer vide order dated 27.04.1993 to
private respondent no. 2.
2. Aggrieved by the order of the Rent Control
and Eviction Officer dated 27.04.1993, the petitioner
moved a revision before the District Judge, Haridwar
being Rent Control Revision No. 01 of 1993. The
Revisional Authority came to the conclusion that the
notices were not sent to the landlord as required under
Section 9(3) of the Act. On this consideration alone, the
Revisional Authority allowed the revision vide order
dated 19.01.2007 and remanded the matter back to the

2
Rent Control and Eviction Officer. This order dated
19.01.2007 has been challenged by the petitioner in the
present writ petition.
3. By interim order of this Court dated
20.02.2007, the operation of the order dated 19.01.2007
has been stayed.
4. From the documents which the present
petitioner has produced before this Court, it seems that
it is not a case where the notices were not issued to the
landlord. It appears that notices were issued to the
landlord and he had also put his appearance, which is
evident from the application moved before the Rent
Control and Eviction Officer on 20.02.1984 and there is
also a finding of the Rent Control and Eviction Officer
that after moving the application requesting that the
allotment be made in favour of Mahesh Kumar
(respondent no. 2 before this Court), he did not appear.
5. So, it is not a case where notices were not
sent to the landlord and therefore the matter was to be
decided on its merit.
6. Consequently, the writ petition is allowed.
Order dated 19.01.2007 is set aside. Let the Revisional
Authority decide the matter on its merit within two
months from the date of production of a certified copy of
this order.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 19.07.2019
